decisions.issues: All four candidates are variants of one base image and share two failures. (1) Wrong setting: on the right side the hold opens onto the storm. There is a bright grating open to the sky, sea spray pours through it, and white water surges in beside the barrels at the lower right. The script needs a closed hold in near darkness, with the storm felt only through the ship's tilt. This also steals the hatch-opening beat from 1.4, and 1.3 establishes a closed deck lit only through its seams. (2) Anatomy: an unbandaged hand with an iron cuff comes out from under Nagoji's right knee, where his right foot should be. It reads as a third hand, and no bare feet with ankle cuffs are visible. v01 also leaves his left forearm bare. v02 to v04 correctly drape the ragged tunic flap over it. What works: Nagoji's face (curled moustache, clean chin with stubble, gold stud), his collar and wrist chain, the chain rising at a slant to a beam ring, the tilt, the pen layout and the clear top-corner caption space.
decisions.correction: Keep the composition, tilt, lighting on Nagoji, his face, collar, wrist chain and pose, and the ragged ochre tunic flap draped over his left forearm (as in v02). Make the hold fully enclosed. The right-hand background must be closed dark hull planking, frames, barrels and more pens receding into shadow. Show no hatch, no grating, no opening to the sky, no daylight, no sea water, spray or rain anywhere in the hold. The only light is a dim hanging lantern glow and thin grey slits at the deck seams overhead, so the hold reads as near darkness and the storm is felt only through the hard tilt and the sliding bodies. Give Nagoji exactly two hands, both bandaged under the iron manacles: one flat on the plank, the other resting near it. No other hand, arm or cuffed limb may come out from under his knees or dhoti. Below his crouched knees, show his two bare feet on the plank with iron ankle cuffs joined by a short hobble chain. Keep plain dark beam or shadow in the top-left and top-right corners for two captions.

decisions.issues: Minor only. Nagoji's collar ring hangs at the front, not the side. His tunic drapes as ragged sleeve cloth over both arms, which reads a little sleeved but keeps the left forearm covered as required. His eyes are fully closed, not half closed. The pen chain runs fairly taut at chest height between the collars instead of drooping onto the plank. The faces, irons, closed hold with lantern glow, Nagoji left and Keshavrao right, and Keshavrao's lock (young, faint moustache, ragged short hair, grey-brown tunic, no stud, thin unbandaged hands) all match. The upper-right wall suits the balloon and the bottom strip over the knees suits the caption. v02 is the same art with no pen chain and a bare left forearm. v01 is rejected: it is set on an open deck in rain with red-waistcoated guards.

Closed deck underside: grey light at the seams, drips, and two running boot shadows. The painted jagged balloons have downward tails that end on the sailors' boot shadows. The tail points above are set at those painted tail tips, the shadows being the sailors' visible trace from above, so the drawn tails cover the painted spikes. If the letterer instead runs tails off the top edge, those white spikes must still be covered. v02 is preferred over v03 because its smaller painted balloons leave both boot shadows fully clear. v01 is rejected: planks are missing, so the deck is open to the sky with boots and rigging in view.

Minor. The guard's raised hand grips the edge of the canvas awning, not the hatch frame. Besides the cross-belt he wears a narrow waist belt (not wide, and no key ring). Faint plank highlights at the far left (about x 0.01 to 0.07, y 0.49 to 0.54) could suggest stencil marks at a squint, but a contrast check shows wood grain, not letterforms. The guard look matches: lean, dark-bearded, steel morion, soaked buff jerkin with cross-belt over a shirt, flintlock in hand, rain pouring through the hatch as the awning is dragged across. v01 is preferred: its small top-left box sits on dark beams clear of the musket hand, while v02's tall left box reaches down to the hand gripping the musket.

Minor only. The ladder is not in frame; the musket lies by the right-hand post, so 'near the foot of the ladder' is implied rather than shown (2.4 shows the ladder). The background prisoners look toward the camera and foreground rather than plainly at the musket, but Nagoji and Keshavrao both look down-right at it. The irons match 1.2: collar-to-collar pen chain through side rings, bandaged wrists under manacles, hobble chains. Nagoji's left forearm is covered by bandage and an ochre flap. Captions go in the top band: beams above the heads, with the right half fully clear. Rejected: v02 (no collars), v03 (no musket), v06 (a deck scene in daylight with a guard). v05, v07 and v08 have Nagoji gazing up and away from the musket. v04 has Keshavrao's second wrist apparently unmanacled and oversized dangling chains. Backup v01 stages the beat best (ladder, beam, every head turned) but has no collar-to-collar pen chain, so it matches 1.2 and 2.3 less well.

Clean. The guard is seen from behind in a morion and buff jerkin with cross-belt, silhouetted in the open hatch against rain and storm light, head turned toward the deck, never looking down. The painted balloons have long tails, but both point at the guard (the correct speaker), and the drawn balloons will cover them. The frame is 2.65:1 and the slot is about 3.97:1, so set visible_rect to roughly [0,0,2043,515] to keep the hatch, guard and beams without letterboxing. v05 is the same art pre-letterboxed to a 5.35:1 strip, which the contain fit would place thinner than the slot. v02 is an outdoor fort scene (reject). v03 and v04 are acceptable but have oversized painted balloons.

Framing is a medium-wide two-shot rather than a 'close' one, which suits the 2.53:1 strip. Keshavrao's eyes are downcast toward the floor, slightly screen-left, rather than clearly toward the musket (screen-right in 2.1). The seawater reads as a wet sheen on the boards rather than a visible threading current. Identity and irons are correct: Nagoji on the left with clean chin, curled moustache, stud, bandaged wrists and left forearm covered; Keshavrao on the right; pen chain collar to collar. Nagoji looks up at the lit hatch stairwell, where rain comes down as in 1.5. v01, v03 and v04 drop Nagoji's wrist bandages, run a chain from collar to wrists, and are 1.5:1, needing a heavy crop. v02 puts an armed guard in the hold (reject).

Minor. The floor carries a shallow sheet of water, and water cascades down the ladder steps, rather than a single thin thread (it matches the 2.3 stairwell). The current does curl around the stock. The flintlock (cock and frizzen visible) lies against the beam, and the ladder rises into grey storm light. The visible strip (y 187-575) is exactly the 5.09:1 slot, with a clear caption band over the dark beams at upper left. v04 is the same art full-frame; it needs a crop to about [0,245,1959,630] and would lose most of the sky. v01 is also acceptable, but its current runs by the barrel rather than the stock, and it needs a heavy crop. v02 is an unrelated scene (reject).

None of the four is acceptable. v01: a guard wades inside the hold (1.5 says no guard enters), hatted crew in red waistcoats at the top of an open ladder with storm light and water pouring down, and a cold blue palette unlike pages 1 and 2. v02: a mid-shot of large foreground figures, not a distant wide. The hold is flooded chest-deep with floating barrels, where the script asks for a knee-deep surge, and no prisoner wears a collar. v03 is the same frame as v04 without the added collar. v04 is the closest, but on the right a breaking wall of sea water rises to the ceiling beams across several bays with no hull planking behind it. That reads as the hull breached and the sea pouring in, which contradicts the knee-deep surge here and the escalation on page 4 (plank only bows in 4.1, 'hull timbers stay whole' in 4.4, waist-deep only in 4.5). The large, detailed foreground figures are not a shot from a distance. There are no plank-shelf pens. Only the far-right man wears a collar: the large foreground prisoner has no collar or manacle, and chains run to wrists and waists instead of collar to collar. Several distant figures wear round dark caps that could be read as guards' helmets. What works in v04: the warm lantern-lit timber hold, matching page 2, and the men thrown sideways with chains whipping sideways.
decisions.correction: Keep the warm lantern-lit wooden hold of v04: heavy timber posts, overhead beams, hanging lanterns, barrels lashed along the sides and the same amber palette as page 2, with the men thrown sideways off balance and the chains whipping sideways. Pull the camera far back to a true distant wide shot from one end of the hold, looking down its length, with the whole image tilted hard as the ship heels. Show plank shelves along both hull sides, split into pens by upright boards, with four or five men in each pen. Every figure is small in frame: no foreground figure and no face larger than a thumbnail. Both hull sides are intact, closed planking, clearly visible behind the pens, and the hatch is closed, with no opening to sea or sky anywhere. The water is a low surge, knee-deep at most, sheeting sideways across the floor between the pens, with spray no higher than a man's waist: no wall of water, no wave reaching the beams, no floating barrels. Every prisoner wears a rigid iron collar, and each pen chain runs collar to collar through the side rings, snapping sideways along the rows and never upward. No chain is fixed to a waist. There are no guards, sailors, helmets or hats anywhere. Keep the top-left corner, about 40 percent of the panel width, as plain dark ceiling beams clear of all heads, for a two-line caption.

decisions.issues: v03 is acceptable, with minor deviations. Nagoji grips the overhead timber with his hands about a forearm apart, not forearms hooked over it with wrists together. His wrist chain sags behind his head, and his collar chain hangs down the centre of his chest instead of drooping to one side. A small bluish grated patch of storm light shows at the upper right. It reads as light through a hatch grating (like the lit hatch in 2.3) and shows no sky or rain. The small painted tail on the right box is only about 40 px and will be covered by the drawn balloon. Rust-brown grime spots on the neighbours' rags are small and read as dirt. Otherwise sound: he shouts down the line, the face matches the sheet (thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud clearly visible), the torn ochre sleeve covers his left forearm, the young neighbour copies the grip with a collar and bare, unbandaged wrists, and three men copy the grip. There is clear space top-left and top-right that covers no face or gripping hand. Rejected: v02 has the best grip, but its right painted tail sticks out about 90 px pointing down at the young man, not Nagoji, and that neighbour's wrists are bandaged. In v06 Nagoji's mouth is closed, so he is not shouting. In v04, v05, v07 and v08 the timber is at chest height, and v04 and v05 add a white under-tunic. v01 is outdoors in front of a fort with guards.

Minor only. A thin black frame border and white margin are painted inside the image (crop them at placement). Nagoji's wrist chain runs longer than a forearm and meets his collar chain near Keshavrao's cuff. There is a small pale window-like patch at the extreme top-left edge. Otherwise sound: the lantern-lit hold matches pages 2 and 3. Nagoji is on the left (thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, ochre rags) and clamps his bandaged hand on Keshavrao's forearm, with the inner forearm turned from camera. Keshavrao is on the right (ragged short hair, faint moustache, grey-brown rags, collar with the side pen chain, bare hands), sliding away and reaching for a barrel. The chain meets his cuff. There is no text, and the panel is silent as the script calls for. Rejected: v02 and v03 show Keshavrao with no iron collar, and v03 also has a bright storm window. v04 puts Nagoji in a white tunic with a red sash. v01 is on the open deck with guards and sky.

No candidate is the tight, face-close two-shot the beat needs, and both lines are Nagoji's. v01 has the right intimacy and water, but it is set against a stone wall with a barred window onto the open sea and rain, not the ship's hold. Neither man wears an iron collar, and the right balloon's tail points at Keshavrao. v02/v03 are wide shots of the pens, with the two men far apart. v04 and v05 have both men hanging from the overhead beam with their heads far apart, so it is not a low-voiced exchange, and v04's right tail points at Keshavrao. v06 is the closest in setting and costume, but the heads are about one and a half head-widths apart, with no water streaming down them and Nagoji's mouth closed. Its right painted tail also sticks out toward Keshavrao's head.
decisions.correction: Keep v06's setting and costumes: the warm lantern-lit hold with timber posts, rope-wrapped pillars and barrels; Nagoji in torn ochre rags with the gold ear stud, clean-shaven chin and thick curled moustache; Keshavrao in grey-brown rags with a faint moustache and short ragged hair; both in hinged iron collars joined by the pen chain drooping between their side rings. Reframe as a tight two-shot from mid-chest up, with Nagoji on the left and Keshavrao on the right, their heads a hand's width apart. Nagoji leans in and speaks low toward Keshavrao's ear, lips slightly parted. Keshavrao listens with his mouth closed and his eyes turned to Nagoji. Seawater streams down both faces and through their hair, dripping from the beams above. Keep Nagoji's left forearm covered by the torn tunic flap or out of frame, and keep Keshavrao's wrists bare under the manacles. Leave the upper-left area above Nagoji as plain dark planking, clear of both faces, for two stacked balloons. Paint nothing on the right half above Keshavrao. If any blank balloon is painted, it sits in the upper left and its tail ends at Nagoji's mouth. No tail points toward Keshavrao.

decisions.issues: Only one candidate, and it fails. The lightning comes through a wide open slot in the wall showing sky, cloud, a drawn bolt and rain, so the closed hold reads as open to the sky. The script asks for a flicker through the seams of the hatch. The lightning does not light half his face: the face is evenly lit in warm tones. The collar ring hangs at the front centre with no pen chain, where the bible calls for a side ring with the chain through it. The middle balloon (Nagoji, off) has a painted tail sticking out toward the RIGHT frame edge. Nagoji sits to Keshavrao's left in 3.3 and 3.4, so that tail stays visible pointing the wrong way. A frame border is painted inside the image. The face, hair, faint moustache, young features and grey-brown tunic are right.
decisions.correction: Keep v01's close framing of Keshavrao alone, with the same face, short ragged hair, faint moustache, wide frightened eyes, grey-brown torn tunic and the dark, gloomy hold planking behind him. Remove the open slot, the sky, the drawn lightning bolt and the rain. The hold is fully enclosed. Instead, thin blue-white lines of light cut through the narrow seams between the closed hatch planks overhead. That cold flash lights exactly one half of his face, the side toward frame right, while the other half stays in deep shadow. Draw his hinged iron collar with its ring at the SIDE of his neck, and the pen chain drooping from that ring out of frame to the left. No ring hangs at the front. Nagoji sits off-panel to Keshavrao's LEFT, as in 3.3 and 3.4, so place Keshavrao's head right of centre with his eyes turned toward frame left. Keep the left 40 percent of the frame as plain dark planking, clear of his face and hands, for three stacked balloons. Any painted tail for the middle balloon runs off the LEFT frame edge, never the right. No painted frame border.

decisions.issues:
v13 is acceptable, with minor notes. It is shot over Keshavrao's shoulder: the back of his short ragged head, his iron collar with a side ring and his grey-brown torn tunic sit in the left foreground. Nagoji crouches in the closed timber hold, jaw set and eyes level on Keshavrao. His bandaged, manacled right fist grips the pen chain, which runs from Keshavrao's collar ring through his fist to his own collar ring. His face matches the sheet: thick curled moustache, clean chin, and only one gold stud visible. The ragged sleeve covers his left forearm, his hands are bandaged, and his ankle cuffs are on a hobble chain. Seawater bursts through the plank seams. There is no sky and no text. Minor points: (1) No plank at the end of the pen clearly bows inward. (2) The short chain between his wrists is not visible, with one fist raised and the other hand on the floor. (3) Above the fist the chain rises to a wall ring at head height beside Keshavrao, not above anyone's head. (4) The rain speckle texture is heavy. (5) The single large painted balloon (tail correctly to Nagoji) will be covered by the letterer, and there is also room upper left.

The others fall short. v01 opens onto sky, rigging and open sea. v02 and v03 are side-by-side two-shots, not over the shoulder, with painted tails aimed at the silent Keshavrao, and v03 has no collars or manacles. In v05, v08 and v09 the upper-left painted tail juts down at the back of Keshavrao's head, the wrong speaker, and v05 also leaves Nagoji's left forearm bare. v10 to v12 are close. In them the pen chain runs from a wall ring to the fist and his collar ring is empty (v12 is the backup).

v01 is acceptable, with minor notes. It is a close shot of Keshavrao matching his sheet: short ragged wet hair, faint moustache, soft young face, grey-brown torn tunic, iron collar and no ear stud. Water runs off him and he wears the ghost of a smile. There is no text, and the upper right is clear for the balloon, whose painted tail points at him. Minor points: (1) There is a faint tuft under his lower lip. (2) The collar ring sits at the front, not the side, with a chain hanging down from it. (3) The plank wall behind him is warmer and brighter than the dark hold of 4.1. (4) A painted black border line runs near the image edges and should crop away.

None of the three is acceptable. v01 shows the hatch wide open to a stormy sky, with a drawn lightning bolt and rain pouring into the hold. v02 and v03 get the lightning right, cold lines of light through the gaps of a closed, grated hatch cover. But their cast is wrong. They include a woman in a head wrap and a young girl, where the script calls for men only. The figures read as a different people from the Indian prisoners of pages 1 to 3. Most wear no hinged collar and no collar-to-collar pen chain. There are no plank shelves or pens, so the panel does not match the hold of the neighbouring panels.
decisions.correction: Keep the v03 composition and lighting exactly: a wide, low view of the cramped timber hold under the deck beams. The hatch cover overhead stays CLOSED, and a single harsh white-blue lightning flash shows only as thin bright lines through the gaps around it and through the plank seams. Keep one blank caption box at top right with nothing inside it. Change the people. Draw ONLY adult men, no women and no children. They are Indian prisoners from Goa of the Konkan and Deccan (Marathi and Konkani men with South Asian features and brown skin, matching the prisoners of the earlier pages). They vary in age and build and wear grey, brown and off-white rags, with no turbans or head wraps. They sit packed onto plank shelves along the curved hull, split into pens by upright boards. Every man wears a rigid hinged iron collar with a ring at the side, wrist manacles on a short chain about a forearm long, and ankle cuffs on a short hobble chain. One slack pen chain per pen runs collar to collar through the side rings and droops along the plank, and no chain hangs vertically above any head. Freeze them like a portrait in the flash: men clinging to beams, posts and each other, mouths open, the whites of their eyes catching the light. No sky, no open hatch, no rain falling inside, and no recognisable Nagoji or Keshavrao.

decisions.issues: v02 is acceptable. The camera looks straight up at the underside of the deck at the moment of impact. The planks bow downward, and sheets of water and grit pour through the seams while the beams and hull timbers stay whole. There are no figures, no text, no sky and no open hatch. The painted blank balloons sit upper left (before the impact) and lower right (after it), with no tails. That is right, because both speakers are sailors off panel above the deck. Both balloons bleed off the frame edges, but the letterer covers them. v01 is rejected: its painted balloon tails point at men in the hold instead of off-panel sailors, the ceiling shows bright openings, and it adds figures the script does not call for.

None of the four is acceptable. v01 is set against stone masonry and a barred window, which reads as the Goa dungeon rather than the ship's hold. It also bares Nagoji's left forearm. In all four, Keshavrao raises one arm high to point while his other manacled hand stays in the water. That breaks the short wrist chain fixed for this chapter and replaces the script's chin jerked upward. v02, v03 and v04 draw no gasping prisoner behind the two men, so the PRISONER line has no speaker. Their first painted tail points at Nagoji or off panel. In v02 to v04 the iron ring on the beam hangs empty, with no pen chain rising to it, which breaks continuity with 5.1, where the chain rises to that ring. v04 is otherwise the closest: the correct wooden hold, waist-deep water, Nagoji's look with bandaged hands and covered left forearm, and Keshavrao shouting into his ear.
decisions.correction: Keep the v04 composition, palette and characters exactly. The wooden hold sits under low deck beams, with water surging waist-deep, pouring through a hull seam at right, and chains dragging heavy through it. Nagoji is on the LEFT: bandaged hands, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, one small gold ear stud, hinged iron collar, and the ragged ochre sleeve covering his left forearm. Keshavrao is on the RIGHT, shouting into Nagoji's ear, with thin unbandaged hands. Make four changes. (1) Keshavrao does NOT raise an arm or point. Both his manacled wrists stay low near the water, joined by their short chain about a forearm long, and he jerks his chin sharply upward toward the ring, mouth open. (2) Add one clearly visible gasping prisoner just behind and between them, left of centre: an adult Indian man in grey-brown rags with a hinged iron collar and manacles, chest-deep in the water, mouth wide open. (3) The iron ring is bolted into the beam overhead at upper right, off to one side. The pen chain rises to it at a slant out of the water from the men's collars, so the ring is visibly anchoring the chain and is not empty. Show dark cracks in the wood around its bolts, and remove the other chains hanging straight down from the beams. (4) Draw two blank white speech balloons with nothing inside. The first, upper left, has its tail to the gasping prisoner's mouth. The second, upper right but clear of the ring, has its tail to Keshavrao's mouth. Both stay clear of faces. No stone walls, no barred window, no sky.

decisions.issues: v02 is acceptable. It shows the ring bolted under the overhead beam, cracks and lifting splinters around the plate, and the chain rising at a slant from out of frame lower left, inside a lantern-lit hold that matches 4.5 and 5.2. Minor points: the plate uses crisp hexagonal nuts that look slightly machine-made, the chain is heavier than the collar chain in neighbouring panels, and the hold looks dry here. The painted box upper left sits over plain beam and gets covered. v01 is rejected because it is set outdoors in daylight with palm trees and a stockade fence, so it is not the closed hold.

v06 is acceptable. The ring hangs from one bolt in a freshly splintered beam, and its chain drops slack into the water at the far end of the row. The row of collared, manacled prisoners is dragged sideways and leans to the left. Nagoji (front left) matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, bandaged hands, hinged collar. Keshavrao (second) matches his. Water pours through the deck seams, and the hull timbers stay whole, as 4.4 requires. The caption box upper left covers only ceiling. The backup v04 is weaker because the ring chain runs taut at a diagonal instead of sagging into the water. v05 is rejected because the hull is smashed open to the sea and rain at right, which breaks 4.4. v03 is rejected because the ring hangs detached from the chain, which anticipates 5.5. v02 is rejected because the lead prisoner is a bearded curly-haired man who reads as a bearded Nagoji, and nobody wears collars. v01 is rejected because it is set outside the ship on open sea with guards on deck.

v04 is acceptable. Nagoji stands waist-deep in the flooded hold, teeth bared, rounding on collared prisoners who cry out in hope with fists raised. He matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean chin, clear gold ear stud, bandaged wrists, collar ring and chain. The upper right is plain dark ceiling, room enough for the balloon. Minor points: the gaps in the upper-left hull show rain and pale light beyond, though no rain falls indoors, and Keshavrao is not shown. The backup v05 is almost identical, but its ear stud is only a tiny dot. v01 and v02 are rejected because they are stone dungeons with a barred window onto palm trees and a Portuguese guard, not the ship's hold. v03 is rejected because the hold is dry with daylight windows, which contradicts the flooding in 5.2 and 5.4.

v04 is acceptable. Nagoji (left) and Keshavrao (right) grip the chain in manacled fists and haul it level toward the camera, feet braced in the flood water. The ring hangs from the beam by a single bolt, and its chain drops behind them without attaching to either collar, so nothing pulls on a neck. Nagoji has the moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud and bandaged wrists. Keshavrao has short hacked hair, a faint moustache and no stud. Both painted balloons sit at upper left over background with tails toward Nagoji, the correct speaker. Minor point: the beam around the ring is not visibly splintered as it was in 5.2. The backup v05 is almost identical, with the second painted balloon over the upper-right background. v06, v07, v08 and v09 are rejected because the ring chain runs down in a V into the collar chain between the two men, so it reads as hanging from their necks. v09 also has a long painted tail across the art. v02 and v03 are rejected because the floor is dry and the ring is bolted to the deck in the foreground, not in the beam. v01 is rejected because it is outdoors in daylight with guards.

v03 is acceptable. The freed chain whips away through a splash in the water between the two men, who stagger apart and look up into the open space overhead. Each still wears an empty hinged collar and wrist cuffs, and the ankle hobble chains are visible above the shallow water. Nagoji matches his sheet (moustache, clean chin, small ear stud, bandaged hands), and his left forearm is covered by the ochre sleeve, so the brand stays hidden. Keshavrao matches his sheet, with no stud. The wide frame suits the full-width row, and the lantern-lit hold matches 5.4. Minor points: Nagoji's wrist chain shows as short lengths hanging from each cuff, the tearing-out of the bolt is not shown, and Keshavrao has a bandage on one hand. The backup v04 (v05 is almost identical) shows deeper water that hides the hobbles, and the chain lies still instead of whipping. v02 works but is a 3:2 frame that would crop badly into a full-width row. v01 is rejected because its four painted boxes would stay blank in a panel with no text, the water is only a shallow puddle, and the empty rings are still bolted to the post.

Minor issues only. The 'its men stare after them' beat is implied rather than staged, because the background prisoners are still bent over their own rings. Nagoji's collar ring sits at the front rather than the side. Everything else matches: both men wear empty collars, manacles and hobbles; Nagoji has his ear stud and a clean chin, and his left forearm is wrapped; the hold is flooded and lantern-lit. There is clear space for balloons over the top-left background and for captions over the water. The v04 and v05 frames are pixel-identical. v01 and v02 were rejected: the floor is dry and no other prisoners are present. v06 was not chosen: its long painted tails cut across Nagoji's head.

Pick is clean. Nagoji stands left, looking up at the hatch; Keshavrao stands right, looking at him. They are thigh-deep, with the ladder behind Nagoji. The musket lies as a dark barrel in the water at lower left. Both men wear collars, manacles and bandages as the bible requires. The hatch shows only a small pale, overcast glow, and the warm lantern light matches 6.1. No backup is acceptable. v01 and v02 show Keshavrao with no collar and no manacles. v04 to v07 show blue daylight sky with white clouds through the hatch, which contradicts the night storm with lightning in 6.5 and 7.1. The v06 and v07 frames are identical.

Acceptable with a small setting quibble: behind the water is a wooden plank rim that reads a little like a trough edge, and his dhoti looks dry above the waterline, although 6.2 has him thigh-deep. In a tight insert with the bottom caption over most of the water, this reads well enough. v03 shows the lock best: the frizzen stands open above a dry, empty pan. The bandaged, manacled hands grip soundly and the forearms are covered or out of frame. v01 was rejected: Nagoji crouches dry beside a tub with his feet out of the water, contradicting the flooded hold, and his left forearm is bare and exposed.

Every candidate is a HIGH angle looking down past Nagoji at Keshavrao, the opposite of the scripted 'low angle up the ladder' that leads into the straight-up POV of 6.5. Keshavrao also stands only ankle-deep, although 6.2 has them thigh-deep. Nagoji's hobble chain is out of frame, so 'the hobble chain cuts every step short' is not shown. Otherwise v06 and v07 got a lot right: Nagoji's likeness and gold stud, a fully wrapped left forearm, the empty collar, the musket under his arm, Keshavrao's look, the flooded lantern-lit hold and the wide 2.6:1 band.
decisions.correction: CAMERA CORRECTION: reverse the camera to a true LOW ANGLE. Put the camera at the waterline at the foot of the ladder and look steeply UP the same narrow, swaying round-rung wooden ladder toward a dark hatch square at the top: rain-dark, no daylight, no blue sky, no guard yet. Draw Nagoji partway up, seen from below. The soles of his bare feet and his iron ankle cuffs should sit on a rung near the camera, with the short hobble chain pulled taut between them to show each step cut short. Both bandaged, manacled hands grip the rungs above him and the musket is clamped under his right arm, its stock knocking a rung. His head is turned down over his shoulder toward Keshavrao, face in three-quarter view, mouth open to speak: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small flush gold ear stud, empty iron collar with a side ring, and his left forearm wrapped from elbow to wrist. Put Keshavrao in the lower-left foreground, THIGH-DEEP in dark water at the foot of the ladder, seen over his shoulder or in three-quarter view looking up, with his own collar, manacles and hobble chain. Keep the warm lantern-lit flooded hold and the painted-and-inked style of the neighbouring panels, and keep the wide horizontal band. Place the small blank balloon reserve over dark timber at the upper left and the large caption reserve over dark deck beams at the upper right, clear of both faces, the hands and the hatch. No lettering.

decisions.issues: Both candidates are photographic or 3D-rendered, with no ink linework and glossy CG wood. That breaks sharply from the painted-and-inked style of 6.1 to 6.4 and 7.1. They also show a staircase with deep flat treads, not the narrow round-rung ladder of the neighbouring panels. The guard is not a pure silhouette: in v01 his coat and sleeves show red, in v02 cream. The composition is right, and the painted burst balloon's tail points correctly at the guard: straight up the ladder, lightning in the hatch, morion brim and crest readable, one hand on the rail, and the musket barrel swinging toward the camera.
decisions.correction: STYLE CORRECTION: render in the same painted-and-inked historical graphic-novel style as the neighbouring panels on this page, with bold black ink outlines, hand-painted colour and warm lantern light on the hold timbers. Do NOT make it photographic, cinematic CGI or 3D-rendered. Keep the composition that worked: Nagoji's point of view looking straight up the same narrow round-rung wooden ladder seen in the previous panels, with rungs rather than a staircase with deep treads, to the open hatch filled with slanting rain and a white flash of lightning. On the top rungs, coming down, is a single Portuguese guard shown as a near-solid black silhouette, with no coat colour visible and no red anywhere. Only the upturned brim and crest of his morion read against the flash. One hand grips the ladder rail and the other swings the musket barrel down toward the camera, the muzzle large in the foreground. Keep one blank speech reserve over the dark timber at the upper right, with a short tail that does not cross the guard's silhouette. No lettering.

decisions.issues: None of the 10 candidates is acceptable. (1) The beat is wrong in every one. In v01 to v05 the musket butt hits the guard's hip or buttock, and his gun hand is not struck at all. In v06 to v10 the guard's lower hand grips the end of Nagoji's musket, so it reads as a tug-of-war, not a blow to the wrist. (2) Nagoji stands on a dry plank floor at the foot of the ladder with at most one foot on the bottom rung. The script puts both men on the ladder, and the hold is thigh-deep at the ladder foot in 6.2 (waist-deep in 4.5). (3) Every candidate is a low-angle heroic close shot rather than side-on and distant. (4) The ladder is rope-lashed with round rungs, unlike the flat-tread companion ladder in 6.5, 7.3 and 7.4. (5) v01 and v02 put the guard in a steel cuirass with red sash, sleeves or breeches, which reads as a redcoat. (6) In v02 to v05 Nagoji's near forearm is bare from elbow to bandage. (7) v06 to v10 have a heavy embossed, filigree-like texture over the pillars, barrels and beams. What works (v05): the lightning and rain in the open hatch, the lamp-lit timber hold, Nagoji's face, collar, wrist chain and hobble chain, the guard's morion, buff jerkin and cross-belt, and his musket spinning away at right.
decisions.correction: Keep v05's open hatch with lightning and rain falling through it, the dark lamp-lit timber hold with barrels and cargo netting, and Nagoji's look: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, empty hinged iron collar, torn ochre sleeveless tunic, cream dhoti, bandaged hands and wrists, short wrist chain, ankle cuffs with a short hobble chain. Keep the guard's steel morion, buff leather jerkin, cream shirt and single cross-belt, with no cuirass and nothing red, and keep his musket spinning away into the dark at the right. Change the camera: a true side-on view from mid-height, far back across the hold, so the whole ladder shows in profile and both men are small, each under a third of the frame height. The hold floor is FLOODED. Black, rippling water covers the entire floor thigh-deep, as on page 6, the foot of the ladder vanishes into it, and no dry planks are visible anywhere. The ladder is the steep wooden companion ladder with flat treads and side rails from 6.5 and 7.4, rising diagonally to the hatch. Nagoji is ON the ladder, halfway up, both bare feet on treads well above the water, the hobble chain hanging between his ankles. He holds his own musket reversed in BOTH bandaged hands, butt up, and drives the butt upward into the guard's wrist. The guard is on the treads just above him, near the hatch, coming down, and the ship's lurch has thrown him off balance. His free hand has come off the rail and flails in the air. His other hand held his musket pointed down at Nagoji, and that wrist is the one the butt strikes from below: its fingers spring open as his musket flies away. He must NOT grip Nagoji's musket. Nagoji's left forearm stays behind the musket stock or under the torn tunic flap. No injury is visible. Render in the clean painterly ink-and-colour style of page 6, with no mosaic, embossed or filigree texture on the timber. Leave a large area of plain, low-detail dark hull or shadow at top-left for caption 1 and a smaller one at lower-right over the water for caption 2, both clear of the figures, the musket and the hatch.

decisions.issues: No candidate is acceptable. v01 is set in a daylit stone shaft with a barred window, not the ship's timber hold at night. Its guard wears red, and Nagoji watches him fall instead of looking away. v02's guard wears a steel cuirass with red-and-white striped sleeves, which reads as a redcoat. v02 and v03 share one impossible composition: Nagoji stands inside the ladder frame with his back against the far treads and a tread passing in front of his dhoti, so he is threaded through the ladder. He leans back calmly with a half-smile instead of pressing himself flat. In both the guard is a fully lit foreground figure with a screaming face, not a dark shape falling past between the rungs. None shows the flooded hold, and none has the stormlight from the hatch that 7.1 and 7.4 use.
decisions.correction: Keep v03's dark timber Portuguese hold with its chains, ropes and warm lamp glow deep in the background, but light the ladder mainly from above with cold white lightning through the open hatch, matching 7.1 and 7.4. No stone walls, no windows, no daylight. Put the camera close, just to one side of the steep wooden companion ladder with flat treads and side rails, at Nagoji's height. Nagoji clings to the FRONT face of the ladder, facing the treads. His chest, belly and one cheek are pressed flat against them, his eyes are squeezed shut and his face is turned away from the fall. Both bandaged, manacled hands grip the same tread, the short wrist chain between them, and his forearms are pressed to the wood with their inner sides hidden. Both bare feet are on lower treads, the ankle cuffs and short hobble chain hanging. Every tread lies between his body and the far side of the ladder; he is never inside or threaded through it. He keeps his thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, long curly hair, empty hinged collar, torn ochre tunic and cream dhoti. Just behind him, the guard drops past as a DARK, backlit silhouette against the lightning, motion-blurred, arms flung out and grasping at nothing. Only the outline of his morion and jerkin reads: no face detail, no cuirass, nothing red. Far below, black flood water glints. No text, no balloons and no caption boxes: this panel is silent.

decisions.issues: No candidate is acceptable. In v01 to v03 the face-down body is a bare-backed prisoner in a dhoti, not the fallen Portuguese guard. v04 and v05 get the body right: the guard face-down in jerkin and boots, his morion beside him, the prisoners pressed back, no blood, and a clean caption area top-left. But the floor is dry planks under a thin sheen, and the prisoners sit and crouch on dry deck. That breaks the waist-deep flood of 4.5 and the thigh-deep water at the ladder foot in 6.2, and nothing can roll him like loose cargo. The floor planks in v04 and v05 also carry a swirly embossed texture at magnification.
decisions.correction: Keep v05's high view straight down the flat-tread companion ladder: the foreground treads, the brass lamp at left, the lashed bales and barrels, the prisoners' positions against the bales and hull, and the plain blank area at top-left for the caption, clear of every face. The hold is still FLOODED, as on page 6. Dark, moving water knee- to thigh-deep covers the whole floor, the lowest treads dip into it, and no dry plank surface is visible anywhere. At the foot of the ladder the fallen guard floats face-down, half submerged, in his buff leather jerkin, cream shirt and boots, face hidden in the water and arms slack. His morion bobs upside down beside him. The current has rolled him against the hull planks like loose cargo, with a small curl of wake along his side. The collared, manacled prisoners stand or crouch in water to their thighs and waists, backs pressed to the bales and hull, away from him. No blood, and no embossed, filigree or mosaic texture on any surface.

decisions.issues: Minor, acceptable. Two small background deck figures read oddly: one on the raised deck at left in a greenish wide-brimmed hat, and a crewman at right in a dark brimmed hat and vest, facing away. Neither looks at Nagoji or reads as a morion-and-jerkin guard. The gold ear stud is tiny. The glass deck lantern is allowed in a Portuguese setting. Otherwise sound. Nagoji matches the sheet: thick curled moustache, clean chin with light captivity stubble, gold stud, long curly hair, empty hinged collar, torn ochre tunic, and a bandaged hand in a manacle with its chain running back to the hidden other wrist. The visible arm is his right, so the left forearm stays hidden. He is half out of the wooden hatch in driving rain, twisted round to shout down at the prisoners' heads in the dark hold. The flat-tread ladder matches 6.5. The painted balloon sits in the low-detail sky at top-right, clear of his face, and its tail points to his mouth. There is no text, blood or noose. Rejected: v01 draws the hatch shaft as stone masonry, not ship's timber. v02 puts a morion-wearing Portuguese guard at the hatch rim beside Nagoji, which the script does not have and which breaks the escape logic.

v01 is the pick. It shows Nagoji thrown against the rail, gripping a line, with the rope coil at his bare feet. His face is on-model: curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud. His collar ring is empty, and the hobble chain is clear. The mast is snapped and leaning with torn canvas. There is a sailor with a knife in his teeth, men at the pump handles, a mixed barefoot crew, and nobody looking at him. The black-and-gold carved stern is close to the Chapter 2 ship. The painted boxes sit over sky at top left and top right. Minor faults in v01: there seem to be two cuffs on his right wrist, and the wrist chain hangs from one cuff without visibly joining the other wrist. A tiny gilt scroll band under the stern gallery is faintly letter-like at high zoom but reads as ornament at panel size. v02 to v06 are one image, and it has two problems: its stern castle reads like a lamp-lit palace, and a chain runs from the collar ring (heavy and down to the wrist in v02), which contradicts the 'empty collar'. v07 to v09 show Nagoji standing and hauling rope like a crewman instead of thrown against the rail, and they have no stern castle.

v02 is the pick. It gives the high angle down the hatch at Keshavrao, and he matches his sheet: short ragged hair, faint moustache, grey-brown tunic, wide eyes. He wears the iron collar with its side ring, his manacled hands grip the top, and his hobbled bare ankles are chained on a rung below. The painted balloon at top right has no tail, and sky and hatch give room for lettering. Minor points: the shaft is lit warm from below rather than by lightning, and the wrist chain is only visible dangling from one cuff. v01 is the same image without the iron collar, which the script requires, so it is rejected.

v08 is the pick. Nagoji is small in the mid-foreground, seen from behind, braced at the rail. His iron collar has the ring at the side, and his visible right wrist is manacled, chained and bandaged, with the left forearm hidden. A lightning-lit wave rears above the ship. The two insets along the bottom show Keshavrao's manacled hands clamped on the hatch rim with the chain between them, and a shattered spar in the sea. The crew have their backs to him. The painted boxes sit over sky and wave crest, clear of faces. Minor points: the sails look intact, whereas 8.1 has a snapped mainmast. One foreground sailor wears a tricorn and waistcoat, which fits the period but is not the head cloths of 8.1. The spar inset does not show the ship's side. v07 and v06 are the same art without the bandage on his hand. v01 to v05 draw Nagoji large, not small, and show Keshavrao's face in the inset instead of just his hands. In v01 a painted box also covers Keshavrao's eyes.

This is the only candidate, and it is usable. The wave crest breaks over the ship's rail and fills the frame, with no figures, no text and no anachronism. Weak points: the frame is 3:2 rather than a narrow strip, so it needs a horizontal crop through the middle band (rail plus curling water). The rail is a light open balustrade rather than the dark solid bulwark of 8.3. The sky is greyer and lighter than the night storm of 8.1 and 8.3, though it can pass as a lightning flash.

None of the candidates is acceptable. v01 and v02 are 3:2 frames going into a 369x115pt strip, and the compositor fits the frame inside the slot, so either would shrink the panel to about half width. v01 has both hands clamped on the rim, so the sword-reach beat is missing, and its hairline graze is painted red and reads as blood. v02 mirrors the hands. v03 and v04 are the same image, and Keshavrao has no iron collar. v05 has no collar and no manacles on Keshavrao, and it adds sailors in tricornes under a full, intact sail. v06 has no collar or manacles, and both hands are on the rim. v07 to v10 are the best art. Keshavrao matches his sheet (hinged collar with an empty side ring, faint moustache, grey-brown tunic, right wrist manacle with slack chain, left hand clamped on the rim), and the upper-left inset shows Nagoji's bandaged, manacled fingers in the coil. But all four paint a second panel border inside the image: black and white rules at y 102-114 and y 641-653 (native px, v09), with bands of rain and sea above and below, and the inset breaks through the top rule. Under the contain-fit compositor this prints as a frame inside a frame, unlike every other panel on the page, which fill their frames edge to edge. Smaller faults in v07 to v10: his right hand reaches flat out over the deck instead of twitching at his side for a missing sword, his mouth is closed on a shouted line, and the graze is not visible. v07 also puts a cream sleeve on Nagoji's arm in the inset. Fallback if regeneration fails: v09 or v10 could be placed through a visible_rect crop of about [16,116,1700,640]. That removes the painted rules and bands and gives exactly the slot's 3.21 aspect, but it leaves the hand and mouth faults.
decisions.correction: Keep the v09/v10 composition and everything in it that works: Keshavrao drenched and half out of the rectangular deck hatch, short ragged hair slicked flat, faint moustache, grey-brown sleeveless tunic, the hinged iron collar with its empty side ring, iron wrist manacles, his LEFT hand (the viewer's right) clamped on the hatch rim, the wet open deck, rigging and grey-white sea behind him under driving rain, and the upper-left inset of Nagoji's bandaged, manacled fingers clawed into the rope coil with the blank caption area inside it. The scene must fill the whole canvas edge to edge as ONE painting, composed as a wide strip of about 3.2 to 1. Draw NO panel border, rule or frame line inside the image, and no bands of rain, sea or cloud above or below the scene. The inset's top and left edges sit flush with the canvas's top and left edges. Move his RIGHT hand (the viewer's left) off the deck: pull it in low beside his right hip, fingers half-closed on empty air where a sword hilt would hang, with the slack wrist chain drooping between the two cuffs so the manacles stay visibly linked. His mouth is open, shouting toward the viewer's left. Add a pale, rain-washed scrape at his hairline in grey-pink, with no red and no blood. Keep the upper right a clear, low-detail area of spray and sky, away from his face.

decisions.issues: Minor issues only. v05 and v06 are the same art; only the size of the painted reserves differs. Nagoji matches his sheet and the chapter 3 row: thick curled moustache, clean chin, small gold ear stud, long curly hair, collar with side ring, bandaged manacled wrists, ankle irons with hobble chain, torn ochre tunic. His arms are extended at the end of the throw rather than mid-heave, so it reads a little like holding the rope. The rope lies short, halfway across, with coils on the wet deck and water pouring off at the scuppers on the right. Keshavrao (collar, manacles, faint moustache, grey-brown tunic, cream dhoti) is already fully out on the deck in front of a raised hatch coaming. In 9.3 he is back half inside the hatch. Each wrist chain dangles from its own cuff rather than visibly linking the pair, and Nagoji's long ochre tunic hem covers most of the cream dhoti. Hands are sound, and there is no text, gore or anachronism. Lettering: the caption goes in the upper left over the storm sky. Nagoji's balloon fits best in the sky and rigging at top centre, between his head and the mast, with its tail to his mouth. The painted box at the lower right will be covered.

Minor issues only. Keshavrao is half out of the hatch with the rope looped in his manacled hands, and the short wrist chain is caught across the rope. He has the collar with its side ring, faint moustache, short hair and grey-brown tunic, and his hands are sound. The rope runs back across the deck to Nagoji's bandaged, manacled hands at the left edge, and the next wave rears on the right with its white edge curling toward the hatch. Nagoji is cut off at the nose by the top edge, so the ear stud is out of frame. Moustache, light stubble and a clean chin show. His ochre cloth drapes over his forearms like sleeves (this keeps the left forearm covered), and Keshavrao's tunic droops over his left upper arm. There is no text and no noose: the loop is at his chest, not his neck. Rejected: v01 (3:2) and v03 have no collar on Keshavrao. v02 has no collar and paints a panel border inside the image, with dark cloud bands above and below.

Minor issues only. This is a medium shot rather than a true wide. The plunging bow is implied by the grey and white wave filling the background rather than drawn. His shin and raised knee rest over and among the coil rather than pressing squarely on it. Nagoji matches: thick curled moustache, clean chin with light captivity stubble, gold ear stud, empty collar with side ring, bandaged manacled hands with the chain sagging between the wrists, and a cream dhoti. The ochre drape covers the far (left) forearm. The rope runs dead straight and taut to the right, into the white water. The two caption reserves sit top-left and top-right, clear of his face and hands. Backup v02 is a truer wide: a sleeveless tunic per the sheet, his dhoti knee on the coil, the ankle cuff with hobble chain, and a better 3:1 aspect. But his left forearm is bare from elbow to cuff (outer side toward camera), so it is weaker on the brand-concealment rule. Rejected: v06 has no collar and the rope wraps a bitt. v07 runs a chain from the collar ring to the manacles, so the collar is not empty. v04 and v05 show hands only, with no knee or coil. v03 has no coil. v01 has a 2:1 frame and is weaker.

Minor issues only. The bandages are stripped into long trailing strips but not visibly scorched, and the palms are only mildly reddened. There is no torn flesh and no blood. Both open palms face the viewer with thumbs to the viewer's right, so the handedness is slightly ambiguous, but it reads naturally at print size. The knee pinning the coil is under the ochre tunic hem here, while in 9.4 v08 the cream dhoti shows at the knee. The staging matches the script. The rope has parted at a frayed end on the coil side of his hands, the free length slides through his open palms toward the rail and the spray at the right, his knee pins the coil, and the manacles are linked by their short chain. The two caption reserves sit top-left over the tunic and top-right over the rain and rigging, clear of the hands. Rejected: v01 to v07 all break the rope between his two hands. v04 to v06 also lack the knee and coil, v07's wrist cuffs are not linked, and v01 and v02 are 3:2.

Minor: the ladder in the hatch reads as intact, not clearly broken, and Nagoji is a medium-size figure rather than 'small' in the frame. Everything else matches: empty hatch with water pouring into the hold, nobody there, empty hinged collar with its ring, wrist chain, hobble chain, reddened open palms trailing bandage strips, and the frayed rope coil at his feet. Face matches the sheet (thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud). His left forearm is covered by the tunic sleeve. The top-right painted box sits over sky and rigging. The other candidates fail. v03 is the same art but with the left inner forearm bare and turned to camera, which breaks the hidden-brand rule. v01 and v02 also show the bare left forearm, and they put a loose bandage strip at his feet where the frayed rope coil should be.

v03 is clean. Tight rain-soaked face on the right: thick curled moustache, stubbled clean chin, gold stud, collar with ring, eyes turned right toward the off-panel hatch. On the left a ragged-edged dust memory shows Deccan riders galloping away with backs turned (anonymous), a saffron pennant with no marks, and a fallen comrade face down beside his fallen horse, with no blood. Both painted boxes sit on the memory, clear of the face. Small deviation: the horse lies down instead of standing riderless. Backup v07 has a standing riderless horse but carries painted black letterbox bars top and bottom that must be cropped out, and its riders are small silhouettes. v04, v05 and v06 fail the 'tight on face' framing (seated full figure). v01 and v02 repeat v03's art at 3:2 and would lose the face or the memory in a full-width crop.

v03: profile at the rail, facing out to sea. Two turns of rope round his chest pulled tight by bandaged, manacled hands, frayed free end trailing, empty collar with ring, joined wrist chain, and a ragged tunic flap and bandage over the far (left) forearm. The splintered, barnacled spar rides the foam. The hobble chain is out of frame because of the waist-up crop, and the spar sits mid-distance rather than directly below. There is open storm sky right of his face for the 'Forgive me' balloon. Rejected: v01 (Portuguese guards on deck, not in the beat), v04 (rope tied to the spar and a hauling pose), v05 (hands on the rail, no knotting), v06 (hands behind his back and no collar), v07 (confused staging with no rail between him and the sea).

v07 is the only candidate whose wrists stay joined by the short wrist chain. It also shows the hobble chain at the ankles, the collar, two turns of rope round his chest with the frayed end trailing, both forearms under tunic flap and bandage, lightning sky, black water, and the ship's rail behind him. Face matches (moustache, clean chin, small gold stud). Caveat: he leaps screen-left with the ship on the right, the reverse of 10.3 where he faces screen-right toward the sea. That break in screen direction is acceptable across the cut, but a horizontal flip would restore continuity if the page reads awkwardly (both forearms are covered, so a flip is safe for the brand rule). Rejected: v02 (arms flung wide, only one wrist chained, rope rising from behind his neck), v03, v04 and v05 (arms spread with separate chain stubs on each wrist, implying a broken wrist chain), v01 (guards reaching from the rail, arms spread), v06 (a wrist chain and ankle chain running back to the ship, a gold hoop at the neck).

v04: underwater just below the white foam of his entry, looking up past him. Collar with ring, gold stud, moustache and clean chin match. Joined manacles and fists at the bottom edge, rope knotted round his chest, and the rope's free end snakes up toward the barnacled, splintered spar without being tied to it. The ship's dark hull heels away beyond. Minor: at extreme zoom a few barnacles have hole patterns that faintly suggest faces, but at print size they read as barnacles. Rejected: v01 and v02 (rope lashed around the spar instead of a free end), v03 (collar drawn split in two floating pieces, rope ends on the spar, 3:2 format), v05 (no collar, reddish marks on the shoulders, spar reads as part of the hull).
